note: Errors found in this leaderboard's data or method, and upstream benchmark changes that forced data to be replaced. Newest first. Add an entry whenever published data is changed for a reason other than a normal source update.

entries.what: ARC-AGI-3 scores under ARC Prize's Provider Adapter harness were stored only for the three newest entries (Claude Fable 5.2, Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 4 Carbon). For older entries only the Standard-harness score was stored, so the best scores were not comparable across models.
entries.fix: Provider Adapter rows added for every model that has them on ARC Prize's result pages. The best ARC-AGI-3 score changed for six models (for example GPT-6 Astra 62.7 to 99.9, GPT-6.1 Sol 52.7 to 96.4, Claude Sonnet 5.5 24.3 to 72.4).

entries.what: Epoch AI re-fitted its Capabilities Index after adding Gemini 4 Carbon (every value moved slightly, for example Claude Fable 5.2 174.24 to 173.44). Its model pages also show higher GPQA Diamond values for Claude Fable 5.2 (94 to 96) and Claude Opus 5.5 (91 to 94).
entries.fix: ECI rows replaced with the current values; the two GPQA Diamond rows updated.

entries.what: RoboDojo Sim, a public robot-manipulation benchmark, was labelled an in-house benchmark, because its description said that Anthropic's results were run internally.
entries.fix: The label is removed and the official RoboDojo leaderboard is now tracked as a source. Anthropic's own runs stay marked vendor-reported. No default ranking changed.

entries.what: 9 BenchCAD Vision2Code scores that the board had copied from vendor system cards and launch charts were stored as independent results.
entries.fix: They are now marked vendor-reported and no longer count in the default ranking. A single score on an independent page can now be marked vendor-reported.

entries.what: Terminal-Bench released version 4.1: the same 66 tasks with stricter verifiers; existing 4.0 submissions were regraded.
entries.fix: 4.1 added as a new benchmark. The 4.0 results are kept under the archived 4.0 board; both versions count as one benchmark family in rankings.

entries.what: Epoch AI revised its MirrorCode scores (for example Claude Opus 5.5 79 to 96) and re-fitted its Capabilities Index again.
entries.fix: Rows replaced with the current values.

entries.what: Arena vision scores mixed two views of the same leaderboard (raw and style-controlled), so 15 models had two different values.
entries.fix: Only the style-controlled values (the leaderboard's default view) are kept; the vision board was re-read from the 2026-11-08 snapshot.

entries.what: Scale released SWE Atlas v1.1 with a new judge; its scores are not comparable with v1.0.
entries.fix: v1.1 added as new benchmarks; the v1.0 boards are kept for reference, marked superseded and excluded from rankings.

entries.what: Kaggle re-scored the FACTS suite on Nov 6; each model's average now covers only the dimensions it was tested on.
entries.fix: FACTS rows replaced with the 7 tracked models that have all four dimensions; 9 older rows for models with partial or no coverage removed.

entries.what: Epoch AI recomputed its Capabilities Index (ECI); every value moved and one entry (GPT-5.5 Instant) was dropped.
entries.fix: All ECI rows replaced with the new values.

entries.what: Reputation summaries, tags and changelog lines used loaded wording (for example 'suspected benchmark gaming', 'nerf', 'dumb'), and 16 quotes contained insults or allegations of misconduct.
entries.fix: Our own text rewritten in neutral, attributed language; those 16 quotes are no longer shown (the opinions still count in the shares). The quoting policy is in the methodology.

entries.what: Changelog 'best-score changes' took the highest value from any source, so vendor self-reported numbers appeared as improvements over independent results.
entries.fix: The changelog now picks the best value with the same source priority as the report (independent > paper > vendor > aggregator).

entries.what: On Nov 4 the Scale Labs HLE-Diamond rows for GPT-6.1 Terra (35.7) and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (20.5) were deleted because the board seemed to have dropped them. The page read was a stale cached copy.
entries.fix: Both rows restored. Artificial Analysis, Vals.ai and Scale Labs pages are now always read with a cache-busting parameter.

entries.what: Artificial Analysis revised the CritPt v2 dataset (Intelligence Index v5.0.1); earlier CritPt v2 values are not comparable.
entries.fix: Old CritPt v2 rows removed (73). 17 models re-read on Nov 4, the remaining 25 on Nov 5.

entries.what: Design Arena changed the evaluation pool of its Blender 3D board.
entries.fix: 16 rows from the old pool removed; only the new preview data is shown.

entries.what: CWE-bench moved to v2 (250 tasks, 185 vulnerability classes), not comparable with v1.
entries.fix: v1 kept for reference but marked superseded and excluded from rankings.

entries.what: Category rankings counted several versions of the same evaluation separately, let one publisher (Vals.ai) dominate the agentic category, and included vendor self-reports by default.
entries.fix: New method: versions merged into benchmark families, one vote per publisher, independent results only by default (see 'How models are ranked').

entries.what: Reputation ranking put models with only 1-2 opinions at the top.
entries.fix: Shares are now shrunk toward the overall average (prior of 10 opinions) and models with fewer than 8 opinions are listed separately.

entries.what: Inkling and Inkling Small were shown as closed models.
entries.fix: Marked as open weights (available since July).

entries.what: Vals.ai upgraded SAGE to v1.1 with a methodology change.
entries.fix: v1.1 scores stored separately from v1.

entries.what: Scores for the original 'Muse Spark' and the non-Pro 'MiMo V2.5' were mapped to the different models Muse Spark 1.3 and MiMo V2.5 Pro.
entries.fix: 7 scores removed; both names added to the ignore list.

entries.what: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index moved from v4.3.2 to v5.0 (9 evaluations), not comparable with v4.3.2.
entries.fix: Both versions stored separately; v4.3.2 marked superseded and excluded from rankings.

entries.what: Initial build: a vendor's self-reported number could be shown instead of an independent result for the same benchmark; ProgramBench mixed two metrics.
entries.fix: Source priority added (independent > paper > vendor > aggregator); ProgramBench split into 'fully resolved' and 'almost resolved'.
